the two mood stabilizers, Li and VPA, regulate the transcription factor CREB and c-fos in a differential way in rat brain and cultured human neuroblastomas cells.
chronic treatment with Li, but not VPR, decreased CREB-phosphorylation in cerebral cortex and hippocampal regions of rat brain.
the mood stabilizer lithium and valproic acid (VPA) differentially regulate brain-region specific phosphorylated CREB (p-CREB) and c-Fos expression in rats.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of CREB and c-Jun by lithium and VPA, and the effects of the drugs on the expression of c-fos in the rat brain.
understanding the mechanism of action of lithium and VPA.
the molecular mechanisms underlying the long-term prophylaxis of BD by LiCl and VPA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
lithium and VPR may act through different pathways to regulate mood and that the regulation of CREB may be relevant to the lithium effect.
the regulation of CREB and c-Jun by LiCl and VPA may be relevant to their long-term prophytic effects in BD.

lithium and VPR may have different mechanisms to exert their mood stabilizing effects in BD.
the transcription factors, CREB, c-Fos and possibly c-Jun, may be involved in the mechanism of action of LiCl and VPA.

lithium and valproic acid differentially regulate the expression of phosphorylated cAMP responsive element binding protein and c-Fos in the hippocampus.
